summary.intent: Take the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony's product launch: analyze the supplier/ERP data drops, find where the launch plan is wrong, and build a general recheck-and-act agent product (later named Lighthouse) with a polished UI for the Head of Procurement and the Senior Buyer before the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses Sunday despite an 'all ok' plan (overbooked art book receipt, failed statue lot, pack rate, sleeve revision, game cards short), and built a versioned poller, LLM extraction, recompute and approval-gated action product. Much of the UI work landed on main (rename, role display, Maren's inbox, Fixed today, flow view branch), but several commits remain unpushed and the live server unrestarted.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) with no webhooks or notifications; the documented way to detect drops is polling and comparing SHA-256 checksums, since files are replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder; .env holds the token and .env.example is committed with an empty token.
The team workflow uses CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md, and Entire checks run on push, uploading checkpoints; Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files changed.
The API server does not load .env on import, so new settings (e.g. buyer title) need a helper that loads .env first or they are missing after restart.

Routine steps like 'Chase once if no answer' (needs routines watching messages awaiting a reply) and 'Ask for a status' (needs shipment routines) are only valid for certain trigger kinds; the server rejects them elsewhere (e.g. 'step 2 cannot be done on open decisions').
Live (:8000) serves the rebuilt web files immediately, but new server endpoints and settings need a restart; the demo runs at ask-soony-demo.stenglein.dev with email in record-only mode.

The lucas new-approach branch contains a pulse-console app with its own server, inbox and email sending that bypasses the duplicate-send guard and record-only mode, so it should not be merged wholesale.
Case flow and routine diagram share the same connector and node components exported from FlowGraph.tsx so they stay visually consistent.

code.finding: New 'How we got here' component renders agent steps (Portal, Reader, Verifier, Prediction, Approval rule, Decision, Then) from each case's own data, omitting steps without data; a two-column snake layout read confusingly so it was changed to a single top-to-bottom column.
Connector (Link) and node box were exported and reused by CaseFlow so case flow and routine diagrams are drawn by identical code.
Pulse-style describe chat on branch jonas/pulse-ui duplicated the existing 'change in your words' box and was reverted from main as a misread of what the team wanted.

workflow: Check what an existing feature already shows before proposing additions; the 'Covered' green line was dropped after finding Launch already marks fine parts.

Take new UI work onto separate branches/worktrees (jonas/pulse-ui, jonas/case-flow) with desktop and phone screenshots against a copy of demo state before merging; a merge made without alignment on intent had to be undone.
Prefer porting a single piece of another branch over merging it, and keep safeguards (skip when no model configured, try/except) when porting.
Rebase on origin before pushing; re-run tests and build after the rebase.
Use headless Chrome screenshots against preview servers on copies of the demo state with background off and emails recorded only, so live data is never touched.
Interviews with Soony staff informed design: the senior buyer preferred a decision view over a chat pipeline, and Maren wanted decisions first plus what is going right.

friction: The portal token was initially empty so the API returned 401, blocking data work until it was provided.
Two UI misreads cost rework: replacing names with roles when the user wanted names plus roles, and building a second chat when the team liked Pulse's flow view.
The first case flow layout (two-column snake) was confusing, with the second row reading right to left.
Reader step first repeated the file name, and the supplier reply fields wrongly listed Boise's late 36,000 cards as a win until switched to confirmed-orders data.
Hooks looked like they hadn't fired because Entire skips checkpoints when no repo files change.
The 'Add step' menu offered steps that the server then refused, making the feature look broken.
Time pressure: the 12:00 hand-in was approaching with commits unpushed.
open_items: Push main (several commits ahead of origin, including the step menu fixes, routine hint and buyer title) and restart live so sign-in choice, Maren's 'Waiting for your OK' and the heartbeat appear.
Decide whether to merge jonas/case-flow (4000003) into main; jonas/pulse-ui chat branch stays parked.
Port Lucas's 'read new documents before verifying' step into runner.run_pipeline after the hand-in (about 20 minutes, with safeguards).
Pitch deck and video still open for the hand-in.
Routines page redesign: compact list rows with one open at a time, a ⋯ menu for Run/Delete/Show code, and duplicate-routine detection.
Support 'send email, then chase once if no answer' on decision routines via a follow-up watching replies.
Optional logo variants (viewfinder with beam) to nod to the Lighthouse name.
Register sender addresses in the portal and send the Karton Nowak art book order (24h offer) and Boise EXW reply through the product.
Ask Lio engineers whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create portal files.
Browser click-through of the flow, chat and linked 'decisions acted on' interactions was not done; only builds and screenshots were checked.
Brief 'Covered' green line was dropped; 'Fixed today' before/after stop times only shown if history holds them.
